propositions: _build_jira_backend constructs an AcliClient without validating that JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, and JIRA_API_TOKEN are present and non-empty, resulting in a backend with empty Basic-auth credentials that fails only at the first API call.
The Cloud adapter lacks the construction-time credential guard that the DC adapter has (via assert_env_ready and transport.py); this is a test-parity gap with the mature DC implementation.

An unconfigured Cloud environment currently builds a live-looking backend that later produces misleading 401/project-not-found errors instead of a clear configuration error naming the missing variables.

_build_jira_backend must validate that JIRA_USER is an email address (contains @ with non-empty local and domain parts) because Jira Cloud authenticates via Atlassian account email as the Basic-auth username; a bare handle silently 401s.
The test test_cloud_build_backend_with_missing_credentials_does_not_fail_loudly pins the current silent-build behavior and must be flipped to assert that BackendEnvError is raised.

test_the_cloud_factory_also_asserts_conformance uses non-email user credentials in its fixture; after the credential guard is added, its monkeypatched settings must be updated to a valid email so the credential check passes and the conformance assertion still runs.
